oficinaAprender.subtituloMecanico: Your training as a mechanic: check-ins and stages for the vehicles you're responsible for.
oficinaAprender.subtituloGeral: One step at a time. Choose Guided mode for detailed instructions, or Self-paced if you'd rather explore on your own.

meusVeiculos.resumo: Here you only see the vehicles assigned to you. Check the car in when it arrives, and log each repair stage (diagnosis, work in progress, etc.) so the shop and the customer can track progress.
passosGuiados: Open Workshop in the menu (your vehicle list, called "My Vehicles").
In the "Waiting" tab, click "Check-in" on the vehicle that arrived.
Click "+ Stage" to log progress (e.g. Diagnosis, In progress, Final test).
Click the vehicle row to see the full timeline and message the customer if needed.
meusVeiculos.desafio: Check in a vehicle assigned to you and log at least one maintenance stage.
meusVeiculos.dica: Final delivery (closing the service) is done by the shop owner or an administrator, not by you.

notasInternas.titulo: Internal notes (talk to the owner without the customer seeing)
notasInternas.resumo: Inside each vehicle there's an "Internal notes" box just for the team — owner and mechanic. Use it for things like "missing a part, already ordered" or to ask a question, without the customer seeing it. It's different from the "Message" button, which talks directly to the customer.
passosGuiados: Open Workshop in the menu and click a vehicle to expand the details.
Scroll to the yellow "Internal notes (not visible to the customer)" box.
Write your note and click Send — the owner gets a notification right away, in the menu bell.
notasInternas.desafio: Write an internal note on a vehicle you're responsible for.

minhaAgenda.resumo: A view of only the vehicles assigned to you: when each one is due, which have checked in and which have been delivered. On the Board, the Hour view shows when each lift is free.
passosGuiados: Open Schedule in the menu.
Use the Board, Month, Day or List views to see what is planned for you.
On the Board, tap "Hour": see when each lift is free and tap a free time to book it for your car.
You can also check in directly from here, same as in "Workshop".
minhaAgenda.desafio: Check your schedule and identify when your next check-in is due.

perfil.resumo: This is your master record: it defines what type of service you handle, your service radius, and what customers see on your public page. Without specialties selected, you won't receive any requests.
passosGuiados: Open your Profile: on a computer, click your name or initial in the top right corner; on a phone, menu ☰ → Profile.
Under "Specialties", select at least one type of service your shop does (e.g. Mechanical, Bodywork).
Fill in address, city, state and service radius.
(Optional) Under "Capacity", enter how many cars fit in the workshop at the same time and, if you like, per type of service. Empty = no limit.
(Optional) Add a logo and photos, and turn on "Car monitoring" to see on the Board how long each car stays in the workshop.
Click "Save Changes" at the bottom of the page.
perfil.desafio: Set up your profile so you start receiving real customer requests: at least one specialty selected and an address filled in.

solicitacoes.resumo: This is the "storefront" of repair requests from customers in your area. You choose which ones to quote. The customer only sees your name and photo until you send a quote — full contact details only appear after they accept.
passosGuiados: Open Requests in the menu.
Click a request in the list to see the details (damage photos, vehicle, description).
Click "Send Quote".
Add the items (description, type, price, quantity). Already have the quote in another system? Tap "Take a photo" or "Choose a file or PDF": the AI fills in the items and you just check them.
Check the total: the customer pays only the quote amount, and BipFix currently charges the garage no commission.
Set the lead time, warranty and the available check-in times, then click "Send Quote".
solicitacoes.desafio: Send a real quote for an open request in your area.
solicitacoes.dica: The faster you respond, the more likely the customer is to pick your quote.

checkin.resumo: Once the customer accepts the quote, the vehicle enters your schedule. You check it in when it arrives, log the repair stages, and confirm delivery at the end.
passosGuiados: Open Workshop in the menu (list of vehicles in service).
In the "Waiting" tab, click "Check-in" on the car that arrived. If your workshop has bays set up, choose the lift or bay in "Put on".
Click "+ Stage" to log progress (e.g. Diagnosis, In progress).
When you're done, click "Delivery" to close out the service.
checkin.desafio: Check in a vehicle (from the platform or manually, via Manual Check-in) and log at least one maintenance stage.
checkin.dica: A car arrived without going through the site? Use More → Manual Check-in and leave "The car is already here" ticked: it goes straight to "in the workshop".

notasInternas.resumo: Inside each vehicle there's an "Internal notes" box just for you and your mechanics — coordination, alerts, questions about the service, without any of it showing up for the customer (unlike the "Message" button, which talks to the customer). When someone writes, you get a notification right away in the menu bell.
passosGuiados: Open Workshop in the menu and click a vehicle to expand the details.
Scroll to the yellow "Internal notes (not visible to the customer)" box.
Write something and click Send.
notasInternas.desafio: Write an internal note on a vehicle currently in service.

comissao.resumo: Using BipFix is currently free for repair shops. In the future there may be a fee — a percentage of each completed job or a fixed amount per job — always announced 30 calendar days in advance. The Commission screen shows the condition that applies to your shop.
passosGuiados: Open More → Commission in the menu.
Check the condition that applies to your garage today: free to use, no commission.
If the fee is performance-based, responding fast, avoiding quote revisions and asking customers for reviews keep your rate lower.
comissao.desafio: Open the Commission screen and check which condition applies to your shop today.

equipe.resumo: If you work alone, feel free to skip this module — nothing on the site requires having staff. But if you have mechanics, you can register them here and even set how many cars each one can handle at once.
passosGuiados: Open More → Team in the menu.
Click "+ New Employee".
Fill in an email, a temporary password, and choose the role (Mechanic or Administrator).
Click "Register" and pass the password on to the employee.
equipe.desafio: Register a mechanic and set a maximum number of simultaneous vehicles for them.

distribuicao.resumo: In the Schedule, the Board shows each mechanic or each bay (lift, floor bay, waiting space) on its own row, with cars drawn over the time they actually spent in the workshop; the plan appears dashed when it differs. The Hour view shows the day hour by hour — who is on each lift and the bookings — so the team can share the lifts.
passosGuiados: Open Schedule in the menu and tap "Board".
In "Workshop bays", add your lifts, floor bays and waiting spaces (each type is explained on screen).
Choose "View by: Mechanic", "Bay" or "Hour". Drag a car to another row (computer) or tap it and choose (phone).
In the Hour view, tap a free time on a lift to book it for a car; drag the booking to change the time. When the car goes up on the lift, use "Put the car on this bay now".
distribuicao.desafio: Add at least one lift and book a time on it for a car in the Hour view.

pecas.titulo: Parts: buy from stores or sell surplus
pecas.resumo: Need a part? Request a quote from partner stores (and even from neighboring shops). And if you have surplus stock, you can also become a supplier and sell to shops near you.
passosGuiados: Open More → Parts in the menu.
In the "Buy" tab, click "+ New Quote Request" and describe the part you need.
Wait for replies from nearby stores/shops, compare price and lead time, and confirm the order you choose.
(Optional) In the "Sell surplus" tab, turn on the toggle to start replying to nearby shops' quote requests.
pecas.desafio: Create a parts quote request for something your shop actually uses day to day.
